requirements.objective: Provide defensible daily emissions assessments and reviewed regulatory submissions for a ceramics manufacturer's pilot covering one plant, three stacks, particulate matter and NOx.

requirements.normalized: Limit the pilot to one plant, three stacks and two pollutants: particulate matter and NOx.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: demonstrate the stated pilot coverage without introducing additional pollutants or plants.

requirements.normalized: Use UTC for permit days and hour boundaries. Accept concentrations already normalized in mg/Nm³ with at most three decimal places, without performing normalization conversions.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: check UTC day boundaries, concentration precision validation and preservation of supplied normalized values.

requirements.normalized: Exclude combustion equipment control, instrument tuning, dispersion prediction, carbon-credit calculation and replacement of emergency alarms.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: review the planned capability inventory against these exclusions.

requirements.normalized: Allow environmental technicians to maintain effective-dated instrument assignments to stack and pollutant, prevent overlapping assignments for the same stack and pollutant, and preserve instrument identity and assignment history.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: reject overlapping assignments and retain historical instrument identities and assignments after changes.

requirements.normalized: Maintain an OFF, NORMAL or STARTUP operating status with a source reference for each stack-hour. Treat a missing status as unknown rather than OFF.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: distinguish an explicitly documented OFF hour from an hour without operating evidence.

requirements.normalized: Retain actor, time, reason and previous values for corrections to assignments and operating status.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: inspect correction history for attribution, timing, reason and recoverable prior values.

requirements.normalized: Exclude OFF hours from emissions averages while retaining their measurements in evidence history.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: confirm that OFF-hour measurements remain accessible without contributing to emissions averages.

requirements.normalized: Allow technicians to record instrument calibration intervals with start, end and reason. Include the start and exclude the end, require end later than start, and preserve attribution and history for records and corrections.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: reject zero-length or reversed intervals and retain attributed calibration correction history.

requirements.normalized: Invalidate an entire five-minute measurement for compliance when any part overlaps a calibration interval for its instrument, regardless of a VALID source-quality flag.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: calibration from 09:02 to 09:03 invalidates the 09:00–09:05 measurement.
Proposed verification: intervals that only touch at an excluded endpoint do not overlap.

requirements.normalized: Allow a technician to preview a CSV containing delivery_id, measurement_id, instrument_id, interval_start_utc, concentration and source_quality.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: preview synthetic files containing all required columns.

requirements.normalized: Require five-minute measurements starting on a five-minute grid, nonnegative concentrations with at most three decimal places, and source_quality of VALID or INVALID. Reject an entire delivery with row-level reasons and no changes for malformed rows, unknown instruments, off-grid times, duplicate measurement identifiers or duplicate instrument-and-interval measurements.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: exercise each rejection condition and confirm that a delivery containing any invalid row makes no changes.
Proposed verification: retain row-level rejection reasons.

requirements.normalized: Treat an identical delivery identifier and content as a no-op, reject changed content under an existing delivery identifier, and prevent later deliveries from silently replacing existing measurements.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: repeat an identical delivery without changing stored evidence, then reject altered content using the same identifier.
Proposed verification: reject attempts to overwrite an existing measurement through a later delivery.

requirements.normalized: Allow quality reviewers to approve measurement corrections naming the original measurement, replacement concentration or quality flag, reason and supporting reference. Preserve raw values and every correction; only the latest approved correction is effective.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: retain raw values and correction history while using only the latest approved correction as effective data.

requirements.normalized: Apply instrument assignments and calibration invalidation to corrected measurements.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: an approved quality correction cannot override calibration invalidation or instrument applicability.

requirements.normalized: Expect 12 five-minute measurements from the assigned instrument for each operating particulate stack-hour. Require at least nine valid measurements after source-quality, correction and calibration checks; otherwise mark the hour insufficient. Also mark an hour insufficient when it lacks an applicable assignment.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: nine valid measurements of 40 and three invalid measurements produce a sufficient hour; eight valid measurements produce an insufficient hour.
Proposed verification: an operating hour without an applicable assignment is insufficient.

requirements.normalized: Calculate particulate hourly means as arithmetic means of valid concentrations. Compare exact calculated values with limits and round only displayed means to three decimal places, with exact halves rounded upward.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: nine valid concentrations of 40 produce an hourly mean of 40.
Proposed verification: displayed rounding does not change classification near a limit, and exact display-rounding halves round upward.

requirements.normalized: Classify a particulate stack-day as BREACH when any sufficient operating hour has an exact mean above 100 mg/Nm³, even if other hours are insufficient or have unknown operating status.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: a sufficient hourly mean of 101 makes the day BREACH despite another insufficient hour.
Proposed verification: unknown status elsewhere does not suppress an established hourly breach.

requirements.normalized: When no sufficient operating hour exceeds 100 mg/Nm³, classify a particulate stack-day as INDETERMINATE if any stack-hour has unknown operating status or any operating hour is insufficient.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: missing status or an insufficient operating hour yields INDETERMINATE when the hourly breach rule does not apply.

requirements.normalized: After applying hourly-breach and indeterminate rules, average operating particulate hourly means equally. Classify a daily mean above 50 mg/Nm³ as BREACH and at or below 50 as COMPLIANT. A fully documented day with all hours OFF is NO OPERATION, without a zero concentration or COMPLIANT classification.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: ten operating hours averaging 40 and two averaging 70 produce a daily mean of 45 and COMPLIANT when all remaining hours are documented OFF.
Proposed verification: twelve operating hours averaging exactly 50 produce COMPLIANT when remaining hours are documented OFF.
Proposed verification: all 24 statuses OFF produce NO OPERATION; one missing status prevents that result.

requirements.normalized: Assess particulate compliance separately for each stack without averaging stacks together, and count STARTUP as operating for particulate assessment.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: STARTUP participates in particulate assessment and one stack's concentrations cannot dilute another stack's result.

requirements.normalized: The signed NOx permit requires exclusion of STARTUP hours from daily compliance assessment. This mandatory statement conflicts with the regulator's direction and is not an established implementation choice.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: retain this conflicting policy statement for manager resolution without treating it as the selected NOx rule.
external_dependencies: Environmental compliance manager resolution of NOx policy precedence.

requirements.normalized: The regulator's current written direction requires inclusion of STARTUP hours in daily NOx compliance assessment. This mandatory statement conflicts with the signed permit and is not an established implementation choice.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: retain this conflicting policy statement for manager resolution without treating it as the selected NOx rule.
external_dependencies: Environmental compliance manager resolution of NOx policy precedence.

requirements.normalized: Withhold official NOx daily classifications until the environmental compliance manager resolves the STARTUP contradiction and applicable NOx limits are supplied and confirmed. Do not infer numerical NOx outcomes from the particulate examples.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: the unresolved state prevents official NOx daily classification.
Proposed verification: define numerical NOx acceptance cases only after policy resolution and limit confirmation.
external_dependencies: Manager resolution of NOx STARTUP policy.
Supplied and confirmed applicable NOx limits.

requirements.normalized: Support NOx measurement intake, calibration checks and hourly evidence preparation while official daily NOx classification remains unresolved.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: prepare synthetic NOx hourly evidence without selecting a disputed daily policy or asserting a numerical compliance outcome.

requirements.normalized: Keep local register maintenance, calibration validation, measurement intake, correction review, evidence preparation and particulate calculation independently plannable without a regulator connection or NOx policy decision. Keep particulate-only submission preparation usable.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: exercise local capabilities with synthetic files and records while portal configuration and NOx decisions remain absent.
Proposed verification: prepare particulate-only reports without requiring live particulate-only portal support.

requirements.normalized: Allow an initial overview grouping by stack or date using an explicitly labeled reversible assumption. Either grouping is acceptable and must preserve classifications.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: changing presentation grouping leaves compliance classifications unchanged.

requirements.normalized: Allow reviewers to prepare versioned daily reports containing operating evidence, valid-measurement counts, hourly means, permitted daily classifications, exceptions and source-record links. Report preparation does not authorize filing.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: inspect particulate report contents and source links using local evidence.
Proposed verification: report preparation does not create filing authorization or issue an unresolved official NOx classification.

requirements.normalized: Mark affected prepared reports stale when relevant measurements, assignments, calibration or operating status change. Recalculation creates a new report version.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: each relevant evidence change marks affected reports stale, and recalculation creates a distinct version.

requirements.normalized: Keep previously submitted report versions immutable and visible. Corrections require separately reviewed amendments linked to the original submission.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: use a synthetic submitted-version fixture to confirm immutability, visibility and separately reviewed amendment linkage.

requirements.normalized: Expose stale reports, insufficient hours, unknown operating statuses, breaches and filing outcomes in the overview. Do not represent missing results as zero.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: display synthetic examples of each required state and distinguish absent concentrations from numerical zero.

requirements.normalized: Integrate authorized particulate-only daily report and amendment filing with the regulator portal and capture filing outcomes, subject to confirmation of the portal contract and particulate-only support.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: after integration details and access are supplied, check an authorized exact particulate report version against the confirmed portal contract.
Live verification cannot be claimed from the supplied brief.
external_dependencies: Regulator endpoint, authentication, credentials and account.
Plant permissions and confirmed particulate-only filing support.
external_effects: Transmission of particulate reports or amendments to the regulator portal.
Creation or update of an external regulatory filing record.

requirements.normalized: Prevent submission of NOx results until the NOx policy contradiction is resolved and applicable limits are confirmed. Any subsequent NOx report or amendment filing also requires a confirmed portal integration and exact-attempt authorization.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: unresolved NOx policy or missing limits prevent any NOx submission attempt.
Proposed verification: resolution of NOx policy alone does not bypass portal-access or authorization requirements.
external_dependencies: Manager resolution of NOx STARTUP policy.
Supplied and confirmed applicable NOx limits.
Regulator endpoint, authentication, credentials, account and plant permissions.
Payload schemas, acknowledgement meanings and duplicate-filing behavior.
external_effects: When all prerequisites are met, transmission of NOx reports or amendments and creation or update of external regulatory filing records.

requirements.normalized: Before every filing attempt, require separate environmental compliance manager authorization specifying the exact report version, stack set, pollutant set and permit date. The brief supplies no execution permission, accounts, credentials or submission authorizations.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: reject attempts with absent authorization or a mismatch in any required scope field.
Proposed verification: preparing a report does not satisfy the authorization requirement.

requirements.normalized: Invalidate filing authorization when relevant evidence changes. Immediately before filing, reject stale or unauthorized versions rather than silently recalculating and transmitting another version.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: evidence changes invalidate the associated authorization.
Proposed verification: an immediate pre-filing check rejects stale or unauthorized versions without substituting a recalculated report.

requirements.normalized: Preserve distinct filing outcomes of rejected, received for review, legally accepted and unknown. Receipt is not legal acceptance. Link every outcome to the attempted report version and authorization.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: preserve all four outcome states and their version-and-authorization links using synthetic outcomes.
Proposed verification: received-for-review status never implies legal acceptance.

requirements.normalized: Record a filing timeout as unknown and perform no automatic retry.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: a simulated timeout records unknown and schedules no automatic subsequent attempt.

requirements.normalized: Require documented resolution of an unknown filing outcome before another attempt, together with the authorization required for every attempt.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: prevent another attempt while the prior outcome is unresolved or undocumented.
Proposed verification: define resolution-evidence acceptance cases once the resolution procedure is established.
external_dependencies: Documented outcome-resolution procedure and acceptable evidence.
Confirmed regulator acknowledgement and duplicate-filing behavior.

requirements.normalized: Enforce role permissions beyond screen visibility: viewers read; technicians maintain registers, operating evidence, calibrations and intake; quality reviewers approve measurement corrections and prepare reports; only the environmental compliance manager resolves NOx policy and authorizes filings.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: exercise allowed and forbidden operations for each role through the underlying operation interface, including attempts bypassing screen visibility.
Proposed verification: only the manager role can resolve NOx policy or authorize filing.

requirements.normalized: Preserve evidence, corrections, report versions, authorizations and consistent classifications across restart.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: restart with representative evidence and report history, then compare persisted records, authorization states and classifications.

requirements.normalized: Label reversible local-storage, CSV-preview-layout and initial-grouping assumptions as unapproved. Describe verification as proposed work because no implementation, executed tests or live portal evidence is supplied.
acceptance_implications: Proposed verification: review planning artifacts for explicit assumption labels and absence of unsupported implementation, test-execution or live-filing claims.

issues.description: The signed permit excludes STARTUP from daily NOx assessment while the regulator's current written direction includes it. Both are mandatory and no precedence ruling is supplied.
issues.question: What documented resolution will the environmental compliance manager establish for STARTUP treatment and the precedence of these NOx requirements?
issues.rationale: The conflict changes official NOx classification and submission eligibility. It does not block NOx intake, calibration checks, hourly evidence, particulate assessment or particulate-only preparation.

issues.description: Applicable NOx limits have not been supplied or confirmed, and no numerical NOx compliance outcome is asserted.
issues.question: What applicable NOx limits and associated comparison criteria must be confirmed before official classification or submission?
issues.rationale: Official NOx compliance cannot be objectively calculated or accepted without its limits. Particulate limits and local NOx evidence work remain independently specified.

issues.description: The portal endpoint, authentication contract, payload schemas, particulate-only support, acknowledgement meanings and duplicate-filing behavior are unknown.
issues.question: What confirmed portal contract covers daily reports, amendments, particulate-only filings, acknowledgements and duplicate attempts?
issues.rationale: These details determine live transmission and interpretation of external outcomes. They do not prevent local reports, calculations, authorization controls or synthetic outcome-state verification.

issues.description: External accounts, credentials, confirmed plant permissions and exact-attempt submission authorizations are absent. The brief explicitly grants no execution permission.
issues.question: Before a live attempt, what approved account and plant access will be provisioned, and where will the manager's authorization of the exact version, stacks, pollutants and permit date be recorded?
issues.rationale: Missing access and authorization block live filing only. The local authorization model and enforcement can be planned and verified with synthetic records.

issues.description: Another attempt after an unknown outcome requires documented outcome resolution, but acceptable resolution evidence, the responsible confirmer and the resolution procedure are unspecified.
issues.question: What evidence and confirmation procedure establish that an unknown filing outcome is resolved before another authorized attempt?
issues.rationale: This determines whether a subsequent attempt is eligible and could create a duplicate filing. Recording unknown, prohibiting automatic retries and all independent local work remain implementable.

issues.description: Users disagree whether the initial overview groups by stack or date, but the source accepts either grouping.
issues.question: Is stack-first or date-first grouping preferred for the initial overview?
issues.rationale: A labeled reversible default resolves presentation planning without changing classifications or requiring customer approval of the assumed choice.

issues.description: Assignments are effective-dated, but the source does not specify whether an instrument assignment may change within a stack-hour or measurement interval, or how such transitions affect the expected measurements and hourly mean.
issues.question: Must assignment changes align to hour or five-minute boundaries, and how should an hour spanning an assignment change select and count applicable measurements?
issues.rationale: The transition rule changes measurement eligibility and objective acceptance of affected hourly calculations. This uncertainty is limited to assignment-transition cases; fixed-assignment examples and other local work remain available.

assumptions.statement: For planning, assume a replaceable local transactional store that can persist evidence and commit or reject a delivery atomically; no storage product is selected.
assumptions.rationale: The source permits reversible local-storage assumptions and requires both restart persistence and delivery rejection without changes.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: The storage design would need revision while preserving atomic intake, history and restart behavior.

assumptions.statement: For planning, present CSV preview as a table of supplied fields with row-level validation reasons.
assumptions.rationale: A tabular preview is a reversible layout choice consistent with CSV fields and required row-level rejection reasons.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: The preview layout would change without altering intake validation or delivery atomicity.

assumptions.statement: Use stack-first initial overview grouping as an explicitly labeled reversible planning default.
assumptions.rationale: Either stack-first or date-first grouping is acceptable in the source.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Change the initial grouping to date-first while preserving calculations, classifications and report identities.

Purpose and operating boundary
source_segments.text: ## Purpose and operating boundary

heading_path: StackProof: industrial air-permit evidence and daily compliance
Purpose and operating boundary
source_segments.text: A ceramics manufacturer needs defensible daily emissions assessments and reviewed regulatory submissions. The pilot covers one plant, three stacks and two pollutants: particulate matter and nitrogen oxides (NOx). Permit days and hour boundaries use UTC. Concentrations arrive already normalized in mg/Nm³, with at most three decimal places; do not perform normalization conversions. The service does not control combustion equipment, tune instruments, predict dispersion, calculate carbon credits or replace emergency alarms. Synthetic measurements, operating logs and calibration records are available. External credentials, accounts and submission authorizations are absent.

heading_path: StackProof: industrial air-permit evidence and daily compliance
Monitoring register and operating evidence
source_segments.text: ## Monitoring register and operating evidence

heading_path: StackProof: industrial air-permit evidence and daily compliance
Monitoring register and operating evidence
source_segments.text: An environmental technician maintains effective-dated assignments of instruments to stack and pollutant. Assignments for the same stack and pollutant cannot overlap. Preserve instrument identity and assignment history. Each stack-hour requires an operating status of OFF, NORMAL or STARTUP, supported by a source reference. A missing status is unknown, not OFF. Corrections to assignments or operating status retain actor, time, reason and previous values. OFF hours do not enter emissions averages, but their measurements remain in the evidence history.

heading_path: StackProof: industrial air-permit evidence and daily compliance
Monitoring register and operating evidence
source_segments.text: Technicians can record instrument calibration intervals with start, end and reason. Intervals include their start and exclude their end; end must be later than start. Any overlap between a calibration interval and a measurement's five-minute interval invalidates that whole measurement for compliance, even if its source quality flag says valid. Calibration records and their corrections retain attribution and history. Register maintenance and calibration validation can be planned using local examples before a regulator connection exists.

heading_path: StackProof: industrial air-permit evidence and daily compliance
Measurement intake and corrections
source_segments.text: ## Measurement intake and corrections

heading_path: StackProof: industrial air-permit evidence and daily compliance
Measurement intake and corrections
source_segments.text: A technician can preview a CSV containing delivery_id, measurement_id, instrument_id, interval_start_utc, concentration and source_quality. Each row represents exactly five minutes, beginning at a multiple of five minutes. Concentration must be nonnegative and source_quality must be VALID or INVALID. Reject the entire delivery, with row-level reasons and no changes, for malformed rows, unknown instruments, off-grid times, duplicate measurement identifiers or two measurements for the same instrument and interval. An identical delivery identifier and content is a no-op; changed content under that identifier is rejected. A later delivery cannot silently replace an existing measurement.

heading_path: StackProof: industrial air-permit evidence and daily compliance
Measurement intake and corrections
source_segments.text: A quality reviewer can approve a correction naming the original measurement, replacement concentration or quality flag, reason and supporting reference. Preserve the raw value and every correction; only the latest approved correction is effective. Corrected data still obey calibration invalidation and instrument assignments. Measurement intake and correction review are independently plannable with synthetic files, without deciding disputed NOx policy.

heading_path: StackProof: industrial air-permit evidence and daily compliance
Particulate assessment
source_segments.text: ## Particulate assessment

heading_path: StackProof: industrial air-permit evidence and daily compliance
Particulate assessment
source_segments.text: For each operating particulate stack-hour, expect 12 five-minute measurements from its assigned instrument. At least nine must be valid after source-quality, correction and calibration checks. Otherwise the hour is insufficient. An hour lacking an applicable instrument assignment is also insufficient. The hourly mean is the arithmetic mean of its valid concentrations. Compare exact calculated values with limits; round only displayed means to three decimal places, with exact halves rounded upward.

heading_path: StackProof: industrial air-permit evidence and daily compliance
Particulate assessment
source_segments.text: A particulate day is BREACH if any sufficient operating hour has a mean above 100 mg/Nm³, even when other hours are insufficient or have unknown status. Otherwise, if any stack-hour has unknown operating status or any operating hour is insufficient, the day is INDETERMINATE. Otherwise average all operating hourly means equally: a result above 50 mg/Nm³ is BREACH, and a result at or below 50 is COMPLIANT. A fully documented day with every hour OFF is NO OPERATION, not COMPLIANT and not a zero concentration. Assess each stack separately; do not average stacks together. STARTUP counts as operating for particulate assessment.

heading_path: StackProof: industrial air-permit evidence and daily compliance
NOx contradiction and review scope
source_segments.text: ## NOx contradiction and review scope

heading_path: StackProof: industrial air-permit evidence and daily compliance
NOx contradiction and review scope
source_segments.text: The plant's signed NOx permit states “exclude STARTUP hours from the daily compliance assessment.” The regulator's current written direction states “include STARTUP hours in the daily compliance assessment.” Both are mandatory, with no precedence ruling supplied. The environmental compliance manager must resolve this contradiction. Do not issue an official NOx daily classification or submit NOx results before resolution and confirmation of the applicable NOx limits. Those limits have not been supplied. NOx intake, calibration checks and hourly evidence preparation can proceed; particulate assessment and particulate-only submission preparation must remain usable. Users also disagree whether the overview should initially group results by stack or date. Either grouping is acceptable and must not change classifications.

heading_path: StackProof: industrial air-permit evidence and daily compliance
Review, revisions and external filing
source_segments.text: ## Review, revisions and external filing

heading_path: StackProof: industrial air-permit evidence and daily compliance
Review, revisions and external filing
source_segments.text: A reviewer can prepare a versioned daily report showing operating evidence, valid-measurement counts, hourly means, daily classification, exceptions and links to source records. Preparation does not authorize filing. Changes to relevant measurements, assignments, calibration or operating status mark an affected prepared report stale. Recalculation creates a new report version. A previously submitted version remains immutable and visible; corrections require a separately reviewed amendment linked to that submission. The overview must expose stale reports, insufficient hours, unknown statuses, breaches and filing outcomes rather than displaying missing results as zero.

heading_path: StackProof: industrial air-permit evidence and daily compliance
Review, revisions and external filing
source_segments.text: The regulator portal is expected to accept daily reports and amendments and return filing outcomes. Its endpoint, authentication, plant permissions, payload schema, particulate-only filing support, acknowledgement meanings and duplicate-filing behavior are unknown. These block live filing, not local evidence preparation or particulate calculation. Before any attempt, the environmental compliance manager must separately authorize the exact report version, stack set, pollutant set and permit date. This brief grants no execution permission. Relevant evidence changes invalidate that authorization. Immediately before filing, reject stale or unauthorized versions rather than silently recalculating and sending a different report.

heading_path: StackProof: industrial air-permit evidence and daily compliance
Review, revisions and external filing
source_segments.text: Preserve distinct filing outcomes of rejected, received for review, legally accepted and unknown. Receipt is not legal acceptance. A timeout is unknown; another attempt requires documented outcome resolution, with no automatic retry. Link every outcome to the attempted version and authorization. Viewers can read; technicians maintain registers, operating evidence, calibrations and intake; quality reviewers approve measurement corrections and prepare reports; only the environmental compliance manager resolves NOx policy and authorizes filings. Enforce permissions beyond screen visibility.

Acceptance and delivery expectations
source_segments.text: Nine valid particulate measurements of 40 and three invalid measurements produce a sufficient hourly mean of 40; eight valid measurements produce an insufficient hour. Ten operating hours averaging 40 and two averaging 70 give a daily mean of 45 and COMPLIANT when all other hours are documented OFF. A sufficient hour averaging 101 makes the day BREACH even with another hour insufficient. Twelve operating hours averaging exactly 50 give COMPLIANT. Calibration from 09:02 to 09:03 invalidates the 09:00–09:05 measurement. A day with all 24 statuses OFF yields NO OPERATION; one missing status prevents that result. No numerical NOx compliance outcome is asserted.

Acceptance and delivery expectations
source_segments.text: Evidence, corrections, report versions, authorizations and consistent classifications must survive restart. Local storage, CSV preview layout and initial grouping may use explicitly labeled reversible assumptions; these are not customer approvals. Describe verification as proposed work: no implementation, executed tests or live portal evidence is supplied.

architecture: Proposed modular local application with separate register, intake, assessment, reporting, authorization and filing components. Local evidence preparation and particulate calculations have no dependency on portal availability, NOx policy resolution or filing recovery decisions. [SRC-631976f7c30b, SRC-770c7c5bd347, SRC-c0c68252514b, SRC-5a5274724381]

Preserve ASM-e3ab0087d502 as an unapproved, reversible assumption: use a replaceable local transactional store for evidence, history, report versions, authorizations and filing records. No storage product or external database service is selected. [SRC-2de81dd61ace, SRC-07177b753682]

Separate immutable raw measurements and correction history from effective measurement views. Determine compliance validity using approved corrections, applicable assignments and calibration overlap; retain OFF-hour measurements. [SRC-b2dbaea5dbc0, SRC-631976f7c30b, SRC-770c7c5bd347]

Proposed particulate assessment component uses exact arithmetic for means and limit comparisons, with rounding confined to display. Keep the unresolved assignment-transition case explicit rather than selecting an undocumented rule. [SRC-6144446ca070, SRC-13e79ecfd92b]

Isolate the unresolved NOx daily-assessment branch. Preserve both mandatory STARTUP statements without choosing precedence; withhold official classifications until manager resolution and confirmed limits. NOx intake, calibration checks and hourly evidence remain available. [SRC-c0c68252514b]

Proposed report snapshots identify their evidence inputs. Relevant changes mark affected reports stale and invalidate associated filing authorization; recalculation produces a new version. Submitted versions remain immutable, with separately reviewed amendments linked to them. [SRC-0106ee922148, SRC-5a5274724381]

Keep filing outcomes, timeout handling and negative authorization checks locally verifiable using synthetic records. Place both portal integrations in external_operation nodes; neither is authorized or available for execution. [SRC-96ef114d4418, SRC-5a5274724381, SRC-07515e150f32]

First-attempt filing prerequisites are represented by unconditional node dependencies. A subsequent attempt additionally requires N6's documented-outcome-resolution check; this is a conditional functional prerequisite, not an optional optimization. Until that procedure is established, subsequent attempts remain disabled. [SRC-07515e150f32]

Preserve ASM-548a5717ab8f and ASM-bb99fc051f1d as unapproved, reversible presentation assumptions: tabular CSV preview with row reasons and stack-first initial grouping. No optional optimization dependencies are proposed. [SRC-2de81dd61ace, SRC-c0c68252514b, SRC-07177b753682]
data_entities: Plant, Stack and Pollutant: pilot identifiers covering one plant, three stacks, particulate matter and NOx. [SRC-96ef114d4418]
